open_points.subject: configuration and credential path traversal failures
open_points.text: “a path that names no component, empty or `/` alone, a file that cannot be read; a component that cannot be opened so, for whatever reason, making the file one that cannot be read”
open_points.question: Are an empty path, `/` alone, and every component-opening failure all to be treated as an unreadable file, producing startup refusal for the configuration and `credential_unresolved` for a credential?
options: Treat every listed case as an unreadable file
Give paths naming no component a distinct invalid-path refusal
Apply the unreadable-file result only to component-opening failures
open_points.default_guess: Treat every listed case as an unreadable file, using the existing consequence of rule 1 or rule 2.

open_points.subject: data-directory bootstrap
open_points.text: “At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory” and “The data directory holds one SQLite database”
open_points.question: What happens when the configured data directory, database, content-addressed areas, or spool area does not yet exist?
options: Create all missing installation storage with private permissions
Refuse startup unless the complete layout already exists
Create subareas only when the data directory already exists
open_points.default_guess: Create the data directory and required storage layout with owner-only permissions when absent.

open_points.subject: data-directory path resolution
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user” and “Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links”
open_points.question: How is the configured data-directory path itself, including its ancestor components, opened, and may the data-directory path or an ancestor be a symbolic link?
options: Walk every component without following symbolic links, including the data-directory path
Allow symlinks in ancestors but require the final data directory not to be one
Resolve the configured path normally and police symlinks only below it
open_points.default_guess: Walk the entire data-directory path component by component without following symbolic links.

open_points.subject: private storage permissions
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.”
open_points.question: What exact ownership, file types, and permission bits make the data directory and each contained file or directory private?
options: Require ownership by the kernel user and no group-or-other permission bits on every entry
Check only the top-level directory for owner-only access
Accept group access when the effective access checks still exclude other users
open_points.default_guess: Require every entry to be owned by the kernel's effective user and to have no group-or-other permission bits.

open_points.subject: unexpected data-directory entries
open_points.text: “The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record, a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and the run spool”
open_points.question: What must startup do with an unknown regular file, directory, device, socket, or other non-symlink entry that is not part of the defined store layout?
options: Refuse startup on every unexpected entry
Ignore private unexpected regular entries but refuse special file types
Ignore all non-symlink entries
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup on an unexpected entry rather than deleting or trusting it.

open_points.subject: exclusive process lock
open_points.text: “At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start.”
open_points.question: What kind of lock establishes exclusivity, and must it be released automatically after a crash rather than leaving a stale marker that blocks future starts?
options: Use an operating-system lifetime lock that is released on process exit or crash
Use a persistent lock file and detect stale owners
Use any mechanism that rejects a simultaneous second process, with stale-lock behavior undefined
open_points.default_guess: Use an operating-system advisory lock held for the process lifetime and automatically released after termination.

open_points.subject: supported filesystem semantics
open_points.text: “file[s] … flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place” and “processes_on(data_directory) <= 1”
open_points.question: What happens on a Linux filesystem that does not provide the locking, atomic-rename, or durability semantics these guarantees require?
options: Probe required filesystem behavior and refuse startup when unavailable
Declare such filesystems unsupported without testing
Define weaker guarantees on such filesystems
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup when the required lock or atomic publication operations cannot be established, while relying on documented local-filesystem semantics otherwise.

open_points.subject: crash-durability boundary
open_points.text: “written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place”
open_points.question: Does “flushed” require durability across host or power failure, including syncing the containing directory after rename, or only completeness across a kernel-process crash?
options: Guarantee process-crash safety only
Guarantee power-loss durability with file and directory synchronization
Use SQLite and filesystem defaults without a stated crash model
open_points.default_guess: Guarantee process-crash safety only; power-loss durability is outside the stated contract.

open_points.subject: file fixture publication
open_points.text: “a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest” but rule 4 specifies “Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file”
open_points.question: Are trial file fixtures subject to the same temporary-write, flush, digest-and-size verification, atomic rename, non-overwrite, and orphan-cleanup rules as value bytes?
options: Treat file fixtures exactly like content-addressed value bytes
Apply rule 4 only to value bytes and spooled files
Define a separate fixture publication protocol
open_points.default_guess: Treat file fixtures exactly like content-addressed value bytes.

open_points.subject: deduplication of spooled files
open_points.text: “Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file … and then renamed into place” followed by “Equal bytes are stored once.”
open_points.question: Does “Equal bytes are stored once” apply to run-spooled files as well as content-addressed values and fixtures, despite spool files having run- and attempt-specific positions?
options: Deduplicate values and fixtures only; keep each spool position separate
Deduplicate spool contents across positions while retaining separate references
Deduplicate only within one run
open_points.default_guess: Deduplicate content-addressed values and fixtures only, and keep each spool position as a separate file.

open_points.subject: failed publication cleanup
open_points.text: “the only trace it can leave is a published file no record names” and “On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names … are removed”
open_points.question: Are unreferenced file fixtures and active-run spool files left by failed calls also removed at startup, and what happens if removal of a temporary or unreferenced content file fails?
options: Remove every unreferenced published artifact and refuse startup if cleanup cannot complete
Remove only the artifacts explicitly named and tolerate cleanup failure
Leave active-run orphan spool positions for retry but remove other orphans, refusing startup on cleanup failure
open_points.default_guess: Leave an active-run orphan spool position only when recovery can retry that exact position; remove all other unreferenced artifacts and refuse startup if that cleanup cannot be completed safely.

open_points.subject: existing store corruption
open_points.text: “a completed file a record names is never overwritten” and “nothing else is [removed]”
open_points.question: What must startup or a store read do when the SQLite database is corrupt, a record names a missing file, a named file has the wrong digest or size, or two persisted facts violate an invariant?
options: Refuse startup on any detected inconsistency
Start and fail only the store call that encounters the inconsistency
Repair or discard inconsistent state automatically
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup on any detected database or referenced-file inconsistency and never repair it automatically.

open_points.subject: startup-check precedence
open_points.text: A18 requires locking, privacy and symlink checks at start, while A03, A16 and A17 independently require other startup checks, but no text orders those decisions against one another.
open_points.question: Which refusal is reported when locking, storage permissions or symlinks and another startup condition fail together?
options: Define one global startup-check order
Run A17 configuration checks, then A18 storage checks, then the remaining startup checks
Permit implementation-dependent reporting when multiple startup failures coexist
open_points.default_guess: Read and validate the configuration first, then acquire and validate the store, then validate tokens and dependencies, then probe the sandbox.

open_points.subject: request serialization order
open_points.text: “Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive”
open_points.question: What observable event defines arrival order when requests are received concurrently or become readable at the same time?
options: Order by a sequence assigned when the MCP server accepts a complete request
Order by connection and transport framing rules
Allow the server scheduler to choose any total order
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonically increasing sequence when each complete request is accepted by the surface and process by that sequence.

open_points.subject: record order within one transaction
open_points.text: “The kernel is one process with one store and one writer” and “Every change is one call … and one transaction inside it”
open_points.question: When one store call creates several records, what determines their distinct positions in the store's one order?
options: Each operation specifies an explicit insertion order for all records it creates
Use a fixed global order by model type and identifier
Expose only a transaction position and an explicit deterministic sub-position
Let database insertion order decide
open_points.default_guess: Give every created record a distinct monotonically assigned position in an explicit per-operation order.

open_points.subject: non-Linux startup behavior
open_points.text: “A release runs on Linux and on no other host” but “Another system … is unsupported: the kernel neither tests for it nor defines what it does there”
open_points.question: Must the kernel or release packaging prevent startup on a non-Linux host, or may it start there with undefined behavior because no host check is made?
options: Refuse startup on every non-Linux host
Prevent installation or launch through release packaging without a runtime check
Allow execution on non-Linux hosts with wholly undefined behavior
open_points.default_guess: Package the release for Linux only and make startup fail naturally or explicitly outside Linux, without probing individual Linux flag semantics.
